Done. Both objects are created in `default` and verified.

**What I created (smallest change, no pre-existing resources modified):**

```yaml
# PersistentVolumeClaim app-pvc
spec:
  storageClassName: manual
  volumeName: app-pv          # pins the bind to the pre-created PV
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  resources.requests.storage: 1Gi
```
```yaml
# Pod app
image: nginx:1.31.5
volumeMounts: [{name: data, mountPath: /data}]
volumes: [{name: data, persistentVolumeClaim: {claimName: app-pvc}}]
```

I matched the PVC's request to the PV's `1Gi`/`RWO`/`manual` attributes (mismatched class or size is the usual reason such a claim stays `Pending`) and set `volumeName` so it binds to `app-pv` rather than any other candidate.

**Evidence the reported outcome is achieved:**

| Check | Observed |
|---|---|
| Claim bound to that PV | `app-pvc` → `Bound`, `VOLUME=app-pv`, `CAPACITY=1Gi`, `ACCESS MODES=RWO`, `STORAGECLASS=manual` |
| PV now claimed | `app-pv` → `STATUS=Bound`, `CLAIM=default/app-pvc`, class still `manual`, policy still `Retain` |
| Pod state | `app` → `Running`, `READY 1/1`, `restarts 0`, scheduled on `benchmark-bind-precreated-pv-3522abee-control-plane` |
| Image is the requested one | spec `nginx:1.31.5`, status `docker.io/library/nginx:1.31.5` (`sha256:05b8cb60…`) |
| Mount location | `mountPath=/data`, `claimName=app-pvc`; inside container `/proc/self/mountinfo` shows `/data` backed by the hostPath PV (`… - tmpfs tmpfs … /app-pv /data`), not the container overlay |
| Volume is really persistent | Wrote `/data/hello.txt`, deleted and re-applied the Pod, and the file was still present in the new container (`-rw-r--r-- … hello.txt`, same 11:45 timestamp) |
| Workload actually functional | `curl http://localhost/` inside the Pod returned `200` |

The Pod was recreated once from the same manifest purely as a persistence test; the durable fix is the PVC↔PV binding, not the Pod.

  volumeName: app-pv          # pins the bind to the pre-created PV
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  resources.requests.storage: 1Gi
```
```yaml
# Pod app
image: nginx:1.31.5
volumeMounts: [{name: data, mountPath: /data}]
volumes: [{name: data, persistentVolumeClaim: {claimName: app-pvc}}]
```

I matched the PVC's request to the PV's `1Gi`/`RWO`/`manual` attributes (mismatched class or size is the usual reason such a claim stays `Pending`) and set `volumeName` so it binds to `app-pv` rather than any other candidate.

**Evidence the reported outcome is achieved:**

| Check | Observed |
|---|---|
| Claim bound to that PV | `app-pvc` → `Bound`, `VOLUME=app-pv`, `CAPACITY=1Gi`, `ACCESS MODES=RWO`, `STORAGECLASS=manual` |
| PV now claimed | `app-pv` → `STATUS=Bound`, `CLAIM=default/app-pvc`, class still `manual`, policy still `Retain` |
| Pod state | `app` → `Running`, `READY 1/1`, `restarts 0`, scheduled on `benchmark-bind-precreated-pv-3522abee-control-plane` |
| Image is the requested one | spec `nginx:1.31.5`, status `docker.io/library/nginx:1.31.5` (`sha256:05b8cb60…`) |
| Mount location | `mountPath=/data`, `claimName=app-pvc`; inside container `/proc/self/mountinfo` shows `/data` backed by the hostPath PV (`… - tmpfs tmpfs … /app-pv /data`), not the container overlay |
| Volume is really persistent | Wrote `/data/hello.txt`, deleted and re-applied the Pod, and the file was still present in the new container (`-rw-r--r-- … hello.txt`, same 11:45 timestamp) |
| Workload actually functional | `curl http://localhost/` inside the Pod returned `200` |

The Pod was recreated once from the same manifest purely as a persistence test; the durable fix is the PVC↔PV binding, not the Pod.
